blocks.h2: When It's Time for a New Water Heater

tiles.h3: Water Is Coming From the Tank
tiles.body: A leaking tank can't be repaired. It will only get worse.
The date is on the label. At that age, plan the replacement before it fails.

tiles.h3: You're Paying for Repairs Every Year
tiles.body: Repeated repairs on an old heater add up fast.
A new bathroom, a bigger family or a soaking tub can outgrow your current tank.

blocks.h2: How We Install Your New Water Heater

steps.body: We ask about people, bathrooms and tubs, then match capacity and recovery.
New shutoff, connectors, an expansion tank where needed, and a check of the gas line and vent.
We drain and remove the old tank, test the new one and show you the controls.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Installs in Elgin Homes
blocks.intro: Water heater installs in Elgin often involve more than swapping one tank for another.

items.body: Older basements can have low ceilings, narrow stairs and tight utility corners. We measure before we quote so the new heater fits with the right clearances.
A new gas water heater venting alone into an oversized masonry chimney may not draft well. We may recommend a liner or a power-vent model.

If your 1990s or 2000s home still has its first heater, replacing it before it fails protects a finished basement. It's also a good time to consider a [tankless water heater](/elgin/tankless-water-heater).

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: No guessing on price or fit.

steps.body: Standard, high-efficiency or tankless, explained plainly.
Heater, parts, labor, haul-away and code updates in one number.
Leaks checked, draft tested and hot water confirmed.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Installation Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: How long does a water heater replacement take?
items.preview: Most standard swaps are done in a few hours.
items.answer: Most standard tank replacements take a few hours. Venting changes, a move to a new spot or a switch to tankless take longer.

items.q: Should I get a gas or electric water heater?
items.preview: Usually match what you have. Gas heats faster if it's available.
items.answer: Usually it makes sense to stay with the fuel you already have. Gas recovers faster and is common in Elgin homes. Switching fuels means new gas or electrical work, which we'll explain if you're considering it.

items.q: What size water heater do I need?
items.preview: Most families do well with 40 to 50 gallons.
items.answer: Most households of three or four do well with a 40 or 50 gallon tank. Bigger households or big tubs may need more capacity or a high-recovery model.

items.q: Can you take the old heater away?
items.answer: Yes. We drain the old heater, haul it away and leave the area clean. It's included in the price.

items.q: How much does water heater installation cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the type and the work around it. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the type and size of heater, the venting and any code updates. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
